title: TermAl rejects a valid `engram source` result when Engram prints its slow-operation warning on stderr (launcher and host source capture)
outcome: When `engram source --root <root> --json` succeeds with a valid JSON v1 envelope but its stderr carries only Engram's own slow-operation warning lines ("warning: <operation> is still running after 10 seconds; attempt=…/…; elapsed_ms=…"), TermAl's test launcher and its host source capture accept the result. They keep the warning text as a bounded diagnostic and do not drop it. Any other stderr content, oversized stderr, or a malformed or inconsistent envelope is still refused as today. source_id validation is unchanged, and Engram's warning itself is not suppressed or lowered.
acceptance: A behavioural test of scripts/test-launcher-input.mjs captureCommitInputStatus: a successful source envelope whose stderr holds only well-formed Engram slow-operation warning lines is accepted, with the warning lines preserved in the captured result or diagnostics; stderr with any other line, or above a fixed byte bound, is still refused with ENGRAM_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE

A behavioural test of the Rust host source measurement (src/engram_source_owner.rs, today 'Engram source measurement emitted stderr'): the same accept and refuse split, with source_id checks unchanged; the version and schema probes keep refusing any stderr unless the same exact warning shape is proven to occur there
No test pins prose beyond the warning's parse shape; existing source-id, envelope and refusal tests stay green
